subject: EU Data Subject Request: export + deletion + controller/processor mapping
messages:
From: Sofie Linde <sofie.linde@greencorp.com>

Cc: peter.simpson@greencorp.com
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data subject request (access + deletion) — account GC-2025-41

Hi Priya,

We have a formal data subject request from an EU resident tied to our GreenCorp account. They are asking for a full export of all personal data you hold about their account and for deletion from your systems after export.

A couple of clarifications we need from Redwood before we proceed:
- Can you confirm whether Redwood acts as a controller or processor for GreenCorp data under the DPA/SCCs?
- What exact fields will be included in the export (e.g., user profile, chat transcripts, embeddings, logs, attachments)?
- What is your deletion timeline and how are backups / snapshots handled?
- We also need a mapping of any downstream subprocessors who may have copies or derived data.

Attached is the formal request PDF from the data subject (greencorp-dsr-request.pdf). Please let us know the identity verification steps you require and an estimated timeline.

Best,
Sofie
Sofie Linde
Data Protection Officer | GreenCorp
From: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Sofie Linde <sofie.linde@greencorp.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data subject request (access + deletion) — account GC-2025-41

Hi Sofie — thanks for the heads up and for sending the request. We can support export + deletion for requests tied to customer accounts. A few quick items so we scope correctly:

1) Controller vs Processor: Under the terms in your DPA, Redwood is generally a processor for customer-provided content and a controller only for account administrative data (e.g., billing contact). We'll provide a short mapping that mirrors the DPA + SCC clauses. If you prefer a formal legal confirmation we can loop in our counsel.

2) Export contents: By default our data export includes: account metadata, user profile fields, chat/message transcripts, attachments references (not binary), and application-level metadata. Embeddings and model-derived vectors are included only if they are stored as customer data (we will flag). Logs (infrastructure logs) are excluded unless they contain PII and are part of the subject's interactions.

3) Deletion timeline: We typically complete deletion within 30 days after verification, with backups removed within 30–60 days depending on the backup window. We will provide a deletion confirmation once complete.

4) Subprocessor mapping: we'll produce a list of subprocessors and indicate whether they receive replicas or derivatives of personal data.

Action items for you: please confirm the scope (full account vs single user ID) and provide identity proof (signed form or government ID redacted per your preference). We also attached a small guidance doc for identity proof.

I’ve cc'd Karthik (privacy/product) and Mina (ops) to propose the export format and retention steps.

—Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Privacy Program Manager | Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai, Sofie Linde <sofie.linde@greencorp.com>
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 13:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data subject request (access + deletion) — export schema and subprocessors

Thanks Priya / Sofie — attaching a lightweight export schema (redwood-export-schema-v1.csv) that shows the default columns we produce. Quick notes: 

- Transcripts: we export full message-level transcripts with timestamps and message IDs. Attachments are provided as filename and mime-type (we do not bundle binary by default; can provide S3 links on request).
- Embeddings: included only if the customer has opted to persist embeddings for search/indexing. We will mark any vector columns as "derived".
- Logs: redacted by default; operational logs are retained for troubleshooting and will not be part of the export unless required and approved by the customer/legal.
- Subprocessors: analytics (MetricFlow Inc.), cloud infra (Hyperscale Cloud EU), observability (TraceWorks). We will indicate whether each subprocessor receives raw content, metadata, or only telemetry.

For the deletion workflow: ops will stage a soft-delete (tombstone) immediately after export, then a hard delete after a 30-day retention window. We need explicit confirmation from GreenCorp to proceed with hard delete.

If GreenCorp prefers a faster hard-delete cadence we can evaluate for sensitive cases, but will need contractual sign-off (exception to the standard SLA).

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Product Privacy Lead | Redwood Inference

Thanks, this is helpful. Confirming scope: full account-level export for the subject (user id: gc-user-84021). We appreciate the export schema — please include embeddings if present and any derived metadata that can reasonably identify the data subject.

About subprocessors: we require a list of subprocessors with the categories of data they receive (raw content, metadata, analytics). Please include sustained contact emails if we need to escalate.

On identity verification: we'll provide a signed confirmation form and a redacted government ID. Please confirm preferred upload method (drive link or secure upload).

Would you also send the formal confirmation text we can include in our records that states "Redwood acts as processor for customer content as defined in the DPA dated [date], and controller only for system-level administrative data" — we will place that in our compliance evidence folder.

Regards,
Sofie

Hi Sofie — thanks for confirming the scope. Next steps and confirmations below: 

1) Identity verification: please upload the signed confirmation form and redacted ID via the secure upload link (shareable one-time URL) — we posted an upload slot to your Drive folder (see related_links). If you prefer SFTP we can provide credentials. Attached is a short identity-proof-guidance.txt.

2) Export format & timeline: we will produce: account metadata CSV, transcripts (JSONL with message-level records), attachments manifest (filenames + mime types), and embeddings CSV if present. Estimated turnaround: 7 business days from receipt of verified request. The export will be delivered as a password-protected archive; we will provide the password via a separate email.

3) Controller/Processor language (for your records): "Per the DPA executed between GreenCorp and Redwood Inference dated 2025-08-01, Redwood acts as processor for customer-provided content and controller for account-administration data (billing contact, account identifiers)." Please treat this as a formal confirmation for evidence purposes; our legal team can provide an executed letter if GreenCorp requires it for audit evidence.

4) Subprocessor mapping: as Karthik outlined, the current subprocessors are: MetricFlow Inc. (analytics — receives aggregated metadata), Hyperscale Cloud EU (infrastructure — may store customer data in region), TraceWorks (observability — telemetry only). We'll produce a signed mapping and indicate which subprocessors store replicas.

5) Deletion workflow: after export we'll soft-delete (tombstone) immediately and schedule hard-delete after 30 days. Backups/snapshots are purged per our backup retention (30–60 days). If GreenCorp requests an accelerated hard-delete, please confirm contractual exception and we will engage CS + Legal.

6) Confirmation of completion: once hard-delete completes we will send a signed deletion certificate.

Action requested from GreenCorp: upload the verified identity docs and confirm whether you want embeddings included (you asked for them — please confirm). Also confirm whether GreenCorp approves the standard 30-day hard-delete window.

If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute DPIA/ops call tomorrow morning to walk through the export and subprocessors.

—Priya
Priya Natarajan
